messages:
alex: noticing a weird pattern - several us-east3 GPU nodes failing to attach with read timeouts. overlay logs show repeated nvme read retry spikes since the 02:00 firmware push. infra-bot fired an alert.
infra-bot: [ALERT] nvme_read_retries > 1000 (us-east3)  12m rolling. see /dash/nvme-read-retries and /runbooks/firmware-rollbacks.md
tokyo-oncall: I see batches of retry bursts tied to janitor scrub and image pulls colliding. pending GPU requests ~42 and attach latencies spiking.
mei: Confirmed correlation: nodes with newer fw v3.2.1 show the pattern, older v3.1.8 are fine. We pushed v3.2.1 to us-east3 last night to address thermal resets.
colin: We should avoid broad rollback unless necessary. Quick mitigations: 1) pause janitor scrub concurrency in us-east3, 2) enable soft qos on nvme (limit read_iops for cleaner pods), 3) mark affected node groups as drainable for reboots.
alex: agree. prioritize pausing scrubs + qos. rollback is last-resort. Post a patch with exact commands.
mei: Hotfix commands (scoped to us-east3 namespace):
```
kubectl set env deployment/janitor JANITOR_SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=3 -n infra-us-east3
kubectl annotate nodes -l nvme_fw=v3.2.1 storage.k8s.amazonaws.com/soft-qos-read=10000
kubectl label nodegroup ng-us-east3-firmw v3.2.1-action=quarantine
```
I'll apply these now.
colin: Also flip image pull cache to local warm-cache mode for 90m: reduces read amplification.
[mei reacts :rocket:]
infra-bot: [ACTION] janitor env patched by mei (JANITOR_SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=3)
mei: applying node annotations now.
tokyo-oncall: after the scrub throttle + qos, iops dropped from 150k -> 52k in ~8m. attach pending down 42 -> 5. Good signal.
alex: what's the risk to disk wear backlog? we are slowing cleanup.
colin: backlog will increase but acceptable for 6-12h if we avoid customer impact. Plan: staggered scrub windows overnight and re-run quota against non-attach nodes.
mei: If this stabilizes, we should schedule a targeted rollback of v3.2.1 only for a small canary nodegroup and run long read tests before rolling further.
finance-bot: estimated cost for temporary cross-region spill to eu-central1 (10% of new GPU launches) ~+$150/hr. Approve for up to 3h for SLO preservation? (ops to confirm)
alex: we'll only spill if attach doesn't recover in 30m. prefer not to incur cost.
colin: telemetry shows 30m steady. recovery trending normal.
tokyo-oncall: noting a false-positive in the alert: threshold tuned too low for this fw's retry telemetry. will adjust alert after postmortem.
mei: filing postmortem ticket and RFC for firmware canary gating: /tickets/PMT-3241 and /docs/rfcs/fw-canary-policy.md
alex: good. schedule retro with firmware, janitor, scheduler owners tomorrow 09:30. thanks for fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
mei: leaving increased sensitivity alerts for 2h. will revert annotations and scrub concurrency after 90m if stable.
colin: I'll follow up with a scrub glide schedule and propose adaptive qos knobs in janitor.
infra-bot: [RESOLVE] nvme_read_retries returned to normal at 1745678918 (measured). Incident flagged for postmortem.
